evidence: Panel: the two NoteStore implementations diverge observably on undo (whole-doc replace vs incremental edits). CodeRabbit: cap the snapshot history. Capping changes nothing about the divergence.

panel.summary: The two NoteStore implementations now diverge observably on undo: MemNoteStore emits a whole-document `replace`, YorkieNoteStore emits incremental `edits`
panel.evidence: MemNoteStore.undo/redo emit `{ type: 'replace', content }` (memory.ts:56, 64), which noteSync applies as a full 0..doc.length replacement (note-sync.ts:32-38), resetting selection/decorations; YorkieNoteStore's undo arrives as incremental `edits`. The interface doc in store.ts:54-58 describes one contract for both. Slides deliberately kept MemSlidesStore on snapshot undo (slides-native-undo.md:44-47), so precedent exists, but the notes engine's non-collaborative path (`src/node.ts` exports MemNoteStore as the public store) now behaves differently from production under the same API.
panel.finding_key: packages/notes/src/store/memory.ts::the two notestore implementations now diverge observably on undo: memnotestore emits a whole-document `replace`, yorkienotestore emits incremental `edits`

coderabbit.detail: **Consider capping the snapshot history.** `undoStack` stores one full-text snapshot per un-batched edit and never drops old entries. A long editing session in a large note keeps every historical version in memory. A fixed cap keeps memory bounded and matches typical editor behavior.
